core/landscape/execution/audit_export_sn: The IntegrityError is not swallowed -- it is bound to conflict and carried structurally out of the handler, and every subsequent path consumes it. If the post-CAS find_winner returns None the exception is re-raised as the explicit __cause__ of AuditIntegrityError('audit-export registry CAS collided without an exact reusable winner'); if a winner is found, conflict decides inserted=conflict is None, which is the durable audit record of whether THIS caller performed the insert. No evidence is lost on any path. The handler is empty of raise and return only because the decision needs a database read that must happen outside the rolled-back begin_nested savepoint, which is why R6's structural test fires. Raising inside the handler is the wrong alternative: this is a compare-and-swap over an immutable audit-export registry where a concurrent identical registration is the expected benign race, and converting it into a hard export failure would discard the reusable winner the CAS exists to find and would make concurrent exporters of the same run fail nondeterministically. The candidate is still proved equal to that winner by _assert_candidate_equals_winner before anything is returned, so a genuine divergence still fails closed.
core/landscape/execution/sink_effect_fin: decoded is Tier-1 persisted audit data: it is the return of decode_sink_effect_returned_result over attempt.evidence_json, and the two lines above this guard have already proved that row's integrity by re-deriving evidence_hash as sha256(evidence_json) and refusing on mismatch. The decode returns a closed union of ELSPETH-owned frozen dataclasses (SinkEffectInspection | SinkEffectCommitResult | SinkEffectReconcileResult, src/elspeth/contracts/sink_effects.py, none subclassed), so discriminating it with isinstance against a concrete class ELSPETH defines is exactly the mechanism ADR-032 decision 1 prescribes. The check protects the member-scoped finalization contract: an inspection envelope is not a result and must never finalize a member, so this arm fails closed with LandscapeRecordError. Dropping it would let an inspection fall through to the descriptor and evidence comparisons below, where SinkEffectInspection's differing field set would raise an opaque AttributeError instead of the audit-integrity refusal the caller must see.

Same hash-verified Tier-1 persisted decode as the guard above it: decoded comes from decode_sink_effect_returned_result over an attempt.evidence_json whose evidence_hash this method has already re-derived and checked. SinkEffectReconcileResult is an ELSPETH-owned frozen dataclass with no subclasses, so this is ADR-032 decision 1 nominal discrimination, not a shape guard on foreign data. The check protects the narrower member-scoped rule that a RECONCILED finalization is admissible only when its kind is APPLIED_WITH_EXACT_DESCRIPTOR; every other reconcile kind means the sink write was not proven to have landed with the exact descriptor and must fail closed. The isinstance arm must come first and short-circuit because SinkEffectCommitResult -- the other admissible member of the union -- has no kind attribute, so testing decoded.kind unconditionally would raise AttributeError on every commit-shaped member finalization.
core/landscape/execution/sink_effect_ide: This is the reject arm of the canonical identity walk, and Enum is an abstract base class, not a concrete type. Every enum member's exact type is its own subclass (SinkEffectState, SinkEffectDescriptorMode, ...), so type(value) is Enum is never true for any real value and rewriting the check that way would silently disable it -- the exact failure mode this rationale must avoid. The check protects sink-effect identity hashing: an Enum member's repr and its wire string differ, so admitting one would let two logically identical publication targets hash differently across releases and break the sink-effect identity that dedupe and reconciliation are keyed on. Failing closed with TypeError forces the caller to convert to the exact wire string first. The surrounding function is a closed allowlist over exact types (type(value) in (str, bool), type(value) is int, type(value) is float); this base-class test is the one place where subclass reach is the point rather than a weakness.

Mapping is a collections.abc abstract base class, so there is no exact-type form of this test; it is the deliberate second arm of type(value) is dict or isinstance(value, Mapping), where the first arm is the exact fast path and this arm admits any registered Mapping. That breadth is required and safe here: the values reaching this walk are Tier-1 ELSPETH-constructed target and metadata payloads that arrive as immutable mapping types from deep_thaw and frozen configuration, and rejecting them would make credential-free identity hashing impossible for exactly the payloads the audit trail must hash. The isinstance does not grant trust: everything admitted here is immediately re-walked key by key, each key proved to be an exact str, each value recursively re-derived into a new owned dict, and the original discarded -- so a structural impostor gains nothing beyond having its contents copied and revalidated.
core/landscape/execution/sink_effect_lif: result is Tier-1 in-process audit data typed as the same closed union of two ELSPETH-owned frozen dataclasses (SinkEffectCommitResult | SinkEffectReconcileResult, src/elspeth/contracts/sink_effects.py, no subclasses), so this is the nominal internal-boundary discrimination ADR-032 decision 1 prescribes rather than a shape guard. The check protects durable diversion attribution: only a commit result can divert its own member ordinal, and a result that did divert must then carry exact diversion_attribution evidence or the method fails closed with LandscapeRecordError. Removing the type arm would send reconcile results down the attribution branch and either record an unattributed diversion or reject a legitimately reconciled member. Both members of the union expose diverted_ordinals, so the class identity -- not attribute presence -- is the only thing that distinguishes them; a structural or duck-typed test could not make this distinction at all.

result is Tier-1 in-process audit data statically typed SinkEffectCommitResult | SinkEffectReconcileResult -- a closed two-member union of ELSPETH-owned frozen dataclasses declared in src/elspeth/contracts/sink_effects.py (both have bases (object,) and zero subclasses). This is nominal discrimination against a concrete class ELSPETH defines, which ADR-032 decision 1 prescribes verbatim as the correct internal-boundary mechanism; the option ADR-032 withdrew was runtime_checkable Protocol structural typing, which this is not. The check protects the sink-effect state transition: only a commit result, or a reconcile result whose kind is APPLIED_WITH_EXACT_DESCRIPTOR, may advance the effect to FINALIZED -- a misclassification would finalize an effect whose write never landed. The isinstance arm must stay first and short-circuit because SinkEffectCommitResult has no kind attribute; reordering the disjunction raises AttributeError on every commit path. Rewriting it as type(result) is would be behaviourally identical today and buys no additional guarantee, so it would move the finding without strengthening the control.
core/landscape/scheduler/dispositions.py: The caught exception is _PendingSinkTerminalMiss, a module-private sentinel (dispositions.py:42) raised only by this method's own body as an in-transaction rollback signal for a singleton pending-sink CAS miss. It is Tier-1 internal control flow: it carries no external cause, never escapes this module, and is not an error being discarded. R6 fires solely because the rule's _is_default_return_value heuristic classes the literal 0 as a silent default. Here 0 is a load-bearing count, not a swallow: the sole caller Processor.mark_sink_bound_scheduler_terminal (src/elspeth/engine/processor.py:5298) raises AuditIntegrityError when terminalized != 1, so a miss is reported loudly one frame up and no audit evidence is lost. Re-raising inside the handler is the wrong alternative because it would break the documented F-04 refusal contract (ADR-030 SS C.4 row 7): a non-matching lease owner -- including NULL -- or a deposed leader epoch must roll the fenced transaction back zero-mutation and return 0 for the caller's invariant check, not crash inside the repository and leave the leader-heartbeat extension half-applied.
core/landscape/scheduler/group_losses.py: This is a module-import-time assertion over ELSPETH's own schema object, not a runtime check on data: _reason_column_type is group_losses_table.c.reason.type, declared Column('reason', String(64)) at src/elspeth/core/landscape/schema.py:1150. It is a Tier-1 nominal invariant, and ADR-032 is explicit that Tier-1 invariants must crash on anomaly -- this one raises TypeError at import rather than at the first truncation. The check protects the derived bound _REASON_MAX_LENGTH, whose stated purpose is that the truncation limit and the DDL cannot drift; without the guard, a column changed to an unbounded type would yield length None and silently disable truncation until a write failed against the real database. Subclass tolerance is deliberate and correct here: Text, Unicode and the dialect VARCHAR types are all String subclasses and all satisfy 'bounded String column', so type(...) is String would pin the assertion to an incidental class identity instead of the property it actually needs, and would reject a legitimate dialect-specific column.
